# @forgesworn/ring-sig

> SAG and LSAG ring signatures on secp256k1: prove group membership without revealing identity, with optional double-action detection via linkable key images.

## Getting Started

Install from npm:

```bash
npm install @forgesworn/ring-sig
```

All public keys are x-only hex (32 bytes / 64 hex characters, case-insensitive), following the BIP-340 convention used by Nostr and Taproot. Private keys are 32-byte hex scalars and must be exactly 64 lowercase hex characters below the curve order; anything else throws `ValidationError`.

The library is ESM-only. Import from the single entry point:

```typescript
import { ringSign, ringVerify, lsagSign, lsagVerify, computeKeyImage, hasDuplicateKeyImage } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';
```

Generate throwaway keys with `@noble/curves` and `@noble/hashes` (both are dependencies of this package). `schnorr.getPublicKey` already returns the x-only public key. Import paths need the `.js` suffix:

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { ringSign, ringVerify } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

const members = Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => {
  const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
  return {
    privateKey: bytesToHex(secretKey),
    publicKey: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)),
  };
});
const ring = members.map(m => m.publicKey);

const sig = ringSign('my message', ring, 1, members[1].privateKey); // signer is ring member 1
ringVerify(sig); // true
```

Full API reference with worked examples: [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt). Version history and migration notes: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/ring-sig/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Key Concepts

### Ring Signatures

A ring signature proves "one of these N public keys signed this message" without revealing which one. The verifier learns nothing about the signer's identity: only that they are a member of the specified ring. Ring size is O(n) in the signature.

### SAG (Spontaneous Anonymous Group)

Pure anonymity. Given a set of public keys, the signer produces a signature that any verifier can check against the ring, but nobody can determine which member signed. Useful for whistleblowing, anonymous attestation, and group membership proofs.

### LSAG (Linkable SAG)

Extends SAG with a deterministic **key image** `I = x * H_p(P || electionId)`. If the same private key signs twice with the same `electionId`, the key image is identical, enabling double-action detection. Different `electionId` values produce different key images, so signatures cannot be linked across contexts.

### Key Images

A key image is a curve point deterministically derived from a private key and an election identifier. Two signatures share a key image if and only if they were produced by the same key for the same election. This enables voting, rate-limiting, and double-spend prevention without deanonymisation.

### Domain Separators

Both SAG and LSAG use domain separation strings (defaulting to `'sag-v1'` and `'lsag-v1'`). The domain is hashed into every challenge, so editing `domain` on an existing signature breaks it. The verify functions take only the signature and read the domain from `sig.domain`; when it is absent they use the default for that scheme. There is no expected-domain parameter, so a verifier that wants cross-protocol isolation must pin it itself: `sig.domain === 'my-app-v1'` for a custom domain, or `(sig.domain ?? 'lsag-v1') === 'lsag-v1'` for the default (an explicit default and an absent field are equivalent). Without that check, a signature validly made under any other domain verifies.

## API Surface

Argument types: `message` is a string (at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes), `ring` is `string[]` of x-only public key hex (2 to 1000 entries, no duplicates), `signerIndex` is an integer in `[0, ring.length)`, `privateKey` is a hex string, `electionId` is a non-empty string (at most 512 UTF-8 bytes), `domain` is a string.

### SAG

- `ringSign(message, ring, signerIndex, privateKey, domain?)`: produce a ring signature. Returns a `RingSignature` object.
- `ringVerify(sig)`: verify a ring signature. Returns `boolean`; never throws, returns `false` for any invalid or malformed signature.
- `RingSignature`: interface `{ ring, c0, responses, message, domain? }`

### LSAG

- `lsagSign(message, ring, signerIndex, privateKey, electionId, domain?)`: produce a linkable ring signature. `domain` is the 6th argument, after `electionId`. Returns an `LsagSignature` object.
- `lsagVerify(sig)`: verify a linkable ring signature. Returns `boolean`; never throws, returns `false` for any invalid or malformed signature. A verifier uses `sig.keyImage` and needs no private keys.
- `computeKeyImage(privateKey, publicKey, electionId)`: signer-side only (needs the private key). Compute the deterministic key image for a key/election pair; equals `sig.keyImage` for a signature by that key in that election. Returns compressed point hex.
- `hasDuplicateKeyImage(keyImage, existingImages)`: constant-time check whether a key image appears in `existingImages: string[]` (hex strings, e.g. stored `sig.keyImage` values). Returns `boolean`. Throws `ValidationError` if `keyImage` is not a compressed point (66 hex characters, `02`/`03` prefix); a non-hex entry in `existingImages` throws a `RangeError`.
- `LsagSignature`: interface `{ keyImage, c0, responses, ring, message, electionId, domain? }`

### Errors

- `RingSignatureError`: base error class
- `ValidationError`: thrown by `ringSign`, `lsagSign`, `computeKeyImage` and `hasDuplicateKeyImage` for validated conditions: ring too small/large, index out of range, duplicate members, private key not 64 lowercase hex or not below the curve order, key mismatch, empty or oversized `electionId`, oversized `message`. A ring entry that is not a valid x-only curve point surfaces the underlying `@noble/curves` error, and a non-string ring entry a `TypeError`.
- `CryptoError`: cryptographic failure inside the library (hash-to-point exhaustion); not expected in practice

### Constants

- `MAX_RING_SIZE`: 1000 members. Exported from the package entry point. `MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` (65536) and `MAX_ELECTION_ID_BYTES` (512) exist in the source modules but are not exported from the entry point.

### Verifier checklist

`ringVerify` and `lsagVerify` check that a signature is internally consistent, not that it is the one you expect. Before accepting, compare `sig.ring` with your expected member set, `sig.message` with the expected message, `sig.electionId` with the expected election (a different `electionId` yields a different key image, which would defeat double-vote detection), and pin the domain as described above. Then call `hasDuplicateKeyImage(sig.keyImage, seenImages)` and record `sig.keyImage`.

## When To Use This

**Use SAG when** you need pure anonymity within a group: no linkability between signatures, no double-action detection. Good for anonymous attestation, whistleblowing, and one-off group membership proofs.

**Use LSAG when** you need anonymous signatures that can be checked for double-action: voting (one person, one vote), rate limiting, or preventing double-spending. The key image links signatures by the same key within the same context without revealing who signed.

**Do not use this library** if you need constant-size signatures regardless of ring size (use a ZK-SNARK scheme instead), sub-group security on a different curve, or post-quantum resistance.

### Dependencies

Only two runtime dependencies, both from the audited `@noble` family:
- `@noble/curves` (secp256k1 operations)
- `@noble/hashes` (SHA-256, byte utilities)
